neighbours.label: the slot just before 'already' / 'yet': a clause contrasting how early it is with what has happened (has, hasn't, 'and' after 'not even ... yet')
fire: The semester has barely started and the students are already exhausted.
I have not even unpacked my bags and my boss is calling me.
By the time the firefighters arrived, the roof had already collapsed.
The concert hasn't begun yet, but the hall is packed.
It is only March and the garden is already in full bloom.
We have not even ordered dinner and the kids want dessert.
When I checked the oven, the bread had already burned.
The new manager has hardly settled in and she is already making changes.
quiet: The semester lasts fifteen weeks and the students take four courses.
I have two bags and a small backpack for the trip.
When the firefighters arrived, they climbed onto the roof.
The concert hall has red seats and a large balcony.
It is a big garden with roses and an apple tree.
We have a table for six and the kids want pizza.
When I opened the oven, the kitchen smelled of bread.
The new manager has an office on the third floor.

notes: card: output promotes already/yet in many languages; peaks on ' and', ' has', ' not', '’t'. probe: 'not even finished breakfast and' 0.92, 'barely noon and I am' 0.62, 'had (already)' 0.42; 'She has two brothers' 0.001.
